definition.simple: The energy something has just because it is moving.
definition.academic: The energy possessed by an object due to its motion, defined mathematically as half the mass times the square of its velocity (KE = 1/2 m v^2).

examples: A thrown baseball soaring through the air.

common_misconceptions: Heavy objects always have more kinetic energy than light ones (forgetting velocity squared factor).
ai_context.tutor_hint: If they double the speed, ask them if the energy doubles or quadruples based on the v squared term.
